evidence.note: Repeatedly preserved best-so-far by copying to versioned files (DM-HS.best, v2-v7, .cur, .alt) and explicitly comparing candidate runs to pick the higher-S3 alignment (e.g. step 175 'Run 14 final 0.280666 best so far, copy alt to main'), never losing the best while exploring.

Distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck': computed improvement rates ('gained 0.008 over 560M iters, ~0.014 per 1B, need 3.3B more, will end ~0.288'), diagnosed plateau at ~0.27-0.28 as a deep local optimum, and recognized parallel runs all converging to the same basin.

Caught that the 'perfect' y2kr-SC alignment only gave S3=0.248 (below 0.55) and that SA dropped NC to 0.09; tracked both metrics against both thresholds and added an NC>=0.32 constraint, later verifying S3=0.5559/NC=0.3199 both pass.
Built its own verify.py to confirm S3/NC independently and reported a precise final scoreboard vs each target (DM-HS 0.282 fails 0.32; y2kr-SC passes both).

Minor weakness: repeatedly relaunched sana3 with too-high T_start and each time rediscovered it 'destroys the solution' before killing — some re-running of a variant whose failure mode was already known, keeping it just short of the perfect anchor.

reasoning: Across a ~318-step optimization horizon the agent maintained an accurate, continuous picture of current S3/NC versus thresholds, preserved best-so-far per deliverable in versioned files, projected improvement rates to conclude approaches had plateaued, and independently verified final scores — squarely matching the level-8 anchor and reaching toward level 10 (logged progression, distinguished 'converging slowly' from 'stuck', never lost the best alignment). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because it occasionally re-launched the same too-high-T_start variant whose destructive failure it had already diagnosed.
